claim: For every integer \(r\ge2\), let \(X_{r,a,b}=\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\) with \(1\le a\le b\). Among the canonical members, \(\dim\operatorname{Aut}(X_{r,a,b})\) is maximized uniquely at \((a,b)=(2r,3r)\), with value \(r^2+\binom{3r-1}{r-1}+\binom{4r-1}{r-1}+\binom{2r-1}{r-1}+1\). Among the terminal members, for \(r=2\) the maximum is \(15\), attained exactly at \((1,1)\) and \((1,2)\); for every \(r\ge3\) it is attained uniquely at \((2r-2,3r-3)\), with value \(r^2+\binom{3r-3}{r-1}+\binom{4r-4}{r-1}+\binom{2r-2}{r-1}+1\).

correctness.rationale: Cox Theorem 4.2 reduces the automorphism-group dimension to a sum of Cox-ring graded-piece dimensions minus the one-dimensional grading torus. Exact weighted-monomial counts give the formulas used in the proof. The canonical and terminal triangles are the Reid--Tai specialization already checked in the ledger and are independently replayed from all local age elements by the bundled script. The symbolic case split proves the maxima and uniqueness; exhaustive monomial/age regression through r=30 matches every formula and equality case.
